title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
summary: Small changes, repeated daily, compound into big results. Focus on systems and identity instead of goals.

notes.text: Habit loop: cue, craving, response, reward.
Make good habits obvious and easy; make bad habits invisible and hard.
Aim to become the type of person who does the thing, not just to hit the goal.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
summary: The ability to focus without distraction is rare and valuable. Build routines that protect long stretches of concentration.

notes.text: Schedule deep work blocks in advance, like meetings.
Shallow work is easy to replicate, so it adds little value.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
summary: A sweeping history of humankind, arguing that shared myths like money, nations and religion let large groups cooperate.

notes.text: The Cognitive Revolution made flexible large-scale cooperation possible.
Agriculture raised population but not necessarily individual well-being.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
summary: How you behave with money matters more than how much you know. Short stories about luck, risk and patience.

notes.text: Getting wealthy and staying wealthy are different skills.
Save for flexibility, not just for a specific purchase.
Luck and risk are two sides of the same coin.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
summary: Explores two modes of thought: fast, intuitive System 1 and slow, deliberate System 2, and the biases that result.

notes.text: Anchoring: first numbers we see skew later estimates.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: Andrew Hunt and David Thomas
summary: Practical advice for writing flexible, maintainable code and growing as a software craftsperson.

notes.text: DRY: every piece of knowledge should have one authoritative place.
Fix broken windows early; small messes invite bigger ones.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
summary: A psychiatrist's account of surviving the camps and the idea that finding purpose is the key to enduring suffering.

notes.text: We cannot always choose circumstances, but we can choose our response.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
summary: A shepherd travels from Spain to Egypt in search of treasure and learns to follow his personal calling.

notes.text: The journey matters as much as the treasure.
Fear of failing is often what stops people from starting.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
summary: A memoir about growing up in a survivalist family and discovering education as a path to self-invention.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
summary: Principles and examples for writing readable, maintainable code, with a focus on naming, functions and refactoring.

notes.text: Functions should do one thing and do it well.
Good names remove the need for most comments.
